title: Rare-event modelling of highly pathogenic avian influenza presence for poultry biosecurity surveillance in Delaware
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) remains a major threat to poultry production and animal-health preparedness, but its rarity makes spatially consistent local surveillance prioritization difficult. This study developed a spatial rare-event modelling framework to transform sparse HPAI detections into 3-kilometre surveillance-priority scores in Delaware and evaluated adjacent-region transfer to Maryland. HPAI presence was modelled using poultry-house infrastructure, wetland and hydrographic proximity, agricultural land cover, topography, and wild-bird occurrence predictors. Model performance was assessed using spatial-block validation in Delaware and transfer to a separate Maryland grid. Elastic-net logistic regression achieved the highest Delaware area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) point estimate of 0.935 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.868–0.986), but discrimination was not statistically distinguishable from ridge logistic regression. The highest-ranked 5%, 10%, and 20% of Delaware cells contained 63.6% (95% CI: 30.8–89.1%), 81.8% (48.2–97.7%), and 90.9% (58.7–99.8%) of the 11 HPAI-positive cells, respectively. In Maryland, the Delaware-trained model achieved an AUC of 0.898 (95% CI: 0.719–0.984) and captured 64.3% (95% CI: 35.1–87.2%) and 85.7% (57.2–98.2%) of the 14 HPAI-positive cells in the highest-ranked 5% and 10%, respectively. Poultry infrastructure provided most of the discrimination (AUC = 0.930); adding environmental predictors increased AUC to 0.935, a difference not statistically distinguishable from zero. These findings support surveillance-priority screening for poultry biosecurity, outreach, and preventive action without attributing disease to individual farms.
journal: Preventive Veterinary Medicine: Regional Studies and Reports

analysis.study_design_and_population: This study developed a spatial rare-event modelling framework to transform sparse HPAI detections into 3-kilometre surveillance-priority scores in Delaware and evaluated adjacent-region transfer to Maryland.

However, the study's limitations include the use of spatial-block validation and the potential for regional variability, which may affect the generalizability of the findings.

title_zh: 特拉华州家禽生物安全 高致病性禽流感 存在的罕见事件模型 监测
source_body_en: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) remains a major threat to poultry production and animal-health preparedness, but its rarity makes spatially consistent local surveillance prioritization difficult. This study developed a spatial rare-event modelling framework to transform sparse HPAI detections into 3-kilometre surveillance-priority scores in Delaware and evaluated adjacent-region transfer to Maryland. HPAI presence was modelled using poultry-house infrastructure, wetland and hydrographic proximity, agricultural land cover, topography, and wild-bird occurrence predictors. Model performance was assessed using spatial-block validation in Delaware and transfer to a separate Maryland grid. Elastic-net logistic regression achieved the highest Delaware area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) point estimate of 0.935 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.868–0.986), but discrimination was not statistically distinguishable from ridge logistic regression. The highest-ranked 5%, 10%, and 20% of Delaware cells contained 63.6% (95% CI: 30.8–89.1%), 81.8% (48.2–97.7%), and 90.9% (58.7–99.8%) of the 11 HPAI-positive cells, respectively. In Maryland, the Delaware-trained model achieved an AUC of 0.898 (95% CI: 0.719–0.984) and captured 64.3% (95% CI: 35.1–87.2%) and 85.7% (57.2–98.2%) of the 14 HPAI-positive cells in the highest-ranked 5% and 10%, respectively. Poultry infrastructure provided most of the discrimination (AUC = 0.930); adding environmental predictors increased AUC to 0.935, a difference not statistically distinguishable from zero. These findings support surveillance-priority screening for poultry biosecurity, outreach, and preventive action without attributing disease to individual farms.
abstract_zh: 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) 仍然是家禽生产和动物健康准备的主要威胁,但其稀有性使得空间一致的局部 监测 优先级变得困难。本研究开发了一个空间罕见事件建模框架,将稀疏 HPAI 检测转换为特拉华州 3 公里 监测 优先级分数,并评估了向马里兰州的邻近区域转移。使用禽舍基础设施、湿地和水文邻近性、农业用地覆盖、地形和野鸟发生预测因素对高致病性禽流感的存在进行建模。使用特拉华州的空间块验证来评估模型性能,并转移到单独的马里兰州网格。弹性网逻辑回归在接受者操作特征曲线 (AUC) 点估计下达到了最高的特拉华面积 0.935(95% 置信区间 [CI]:0.868–0.986),但区分度与岭逻辑回归在统计上没有区别。排名最高的 5%、10% 和 20% 特拉华细胞分别包含 11 个 HPAI 阳性细胞的 63.6%(95% CI:30.8-89.1%)、81.8%(48.2-97.7%)和 90.9%(58.7-99.8%)。在马里兰州,特拉华州训练的模型的 AUC 为 0.898 (95% CI: 0.719–0.984),并分别捕获了排名最高的 5% 和 10% 中 14 个 HPAI 阳性细胞的 64.3% (95% CI: 35.1–87.2%) 和 85.7% (57.2–98.2%)。家禽基础设施提供了大部分歧视(AUC = 0.930);添加环境预测因子将 AUC 增加到 0.935,这一差异在统计上与零无法区分。这些发现支持对家禽生物安全、外展和预防行动进行 监测 优先筛查,而不将疾病归因于各个农场。

title: Antibodies targeting a conserved cryptic epitope at the influenza hemagglutinin head-stem interface via distinct binding modes
abstract: Influenza A virus continues to pose pandemic threats, as demonstrated by the recent global spread of highly pathogenic H5N1 strains. Consequently, the development and characterization of vaccines targeting zoonotic influenza subtypes have become a major focus of the field. In this study, we characterize two broadly reactive antibodies previously isolated from H5N1 vaccinees. Although they have distinct immunoglobulin germline gene usage and binding modes, cryo-EM analysis shows that both antibodies share a highly conserved cryptic epitope at the interface of the hemagglutinin (HA) head and stem domains. The antigenicity of this epitope is influenced by natural amino acid variation at residue 293 of HA subunit 1, and its access is facilitated by acid-induced conformational change of HA. Nevertheless, both antibodies are non-neutralizing and possess only marginal protective efficacy against seasonal and H5N1 viruses in vivo, thus representing suboptimal vaccine responses. Overall, our findings expand the interactions of cross-reactive antibodies with an under-characterized HA epitope and provide insights for next-generation influenza vaccine design.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to characterize broadly reactive antibodies against avian influenza A viruses, as these viruses continue to pose pandemic threats due to their global spread, particularly with highly pathogenic H5N1 strains.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved characterizing two broadly reactive antibodies previously isolated from H5N1 vaccinees, focusing on their interaction with avian influenza A viruses and related zoonotic subtypes.
analysis.methods: The study utilized cryo-EM analysis to examine the binding modes of the antibodies and their interaction with the hemagglutinin (HA) head and stem domains of avian influenza A viruses.
analysis.main_results: Both antibodies share a highly conserved cryptic epitope at the HA head-stem interface, despite having distinct immunoglobulin germline gene usage and binding modes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal a previously under-characterized HA epitope that is targeted by cross-reactive antibodies, offering new insights for the development of next-generation influenza vaccines.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform the design of more effective vaccines against avian influenza A viruses, particularly H5N1, by targeting conserved epitopes that may enhance cross-reactivity and protective efficacy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are based on in vivo protective efficacy assessments, which are limited in scope and may not fully capture the complexities of immune responses in different host contexts.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterizes two broadly reactive antibodies against avian influenza A viruses, specifically H5N1, that target a conserved cryptic epitope at the hemagglutinin head-stem interface. The antibodies, despite differing in germline gene usage and binding modes, share this epitope, which is influenced by amino acid variation at residue 293 and is accessible due to acid-induced conformational changes. The findings expand understanding of cross-reactive antibody interactions with this under-characterized epitope, providing insights for improved vaccine design. However, the antibodies are non-neutralizing and show only marginal protective efficacy in vivo, indicating suboptimal vaccine responses. The study's evidence is based on cryo-EM analysis and in vivo testing, which may limit the generalizability of the results. The research contributes to the development of vaccines targeting avian influenza subtypes, particularly those with zoonotic potential, by highlighting a conserved epitope that could be exploited for broader immunity.

abstract_zh: 甲型流感病毒继续构成大流行威胁,最近高致病性 H5N1 病毒株在全球的传播就证明了这一点。因此,针对人畜共患流感亚型的 疫苗 的开发和表征已成为该领域的主要焦点。在这项研究中,我们表征了之前从 H5N1 疫苗 中分离出的两种具有广泛反应性的抗体。尽管它们具有不同的免疫球蛋白种系基因使用和结合模式,但冷冻电镜分析表明,两种抗体在血凝素 (HA) 头和干结构域的界面上共享高度保守的隐藏表位。该表位的抗原性受到 HA 亚基 1 残基 293 处天然氨基酸变异的影响,酸诱导的 HA 构象变化促进了其进入。然而,这两种抗体都不是中和性的,并且对体内季节性病毒和 H5N1 病毒仅具有有限的保护功效,因此代表了次优的 疫苗 反应。总体而言,我们的研究结果扩大了交叉反应抗体与未充分表征的 HA 表位的相互作用,并为下一代流感 疫苗 设计提供了见解。

analysis_zh.main_results: 尽管两种抗体具有不同的免疫球蛋白种系基因使用和结合模式,但它们在 HA 头-茎界面上共享一个高度保守的隐藏表位。

title: Multivalent antiviral conjugates enhance activity against Influenza via cross-linking viruses
abstract: Abstract Long-acting drug–Fc conjugate (CD388) has emerged as a new class of antivirals against influenza A and B, yet the mechanisms governing how Fc conjugation reshapes small-molecule function remain undefined. Here we establish a programmable multivalent antiviral conjugates (AVCs) platform by click chemistry that enables flexible combination of valencies and conjugated drugs, allowing systematic interrogation of valency-dependent antiviral mechanisms. Using zanamivir as a model, mono-, di-, and trivalent zanamivir are conjugated with Fc, with trivalent zanamivir-Fc conjugates (AVC-Z3) exhibiting higher activity than lower-valent AVCs. AVC-Z3 induces inter-virion aggregation, thereby coupling blockade of viral entry with restriction of viral release. This cross-linking–mediated dual-stage inhibition represents a mechanistic shift from neuraminidase suppression to physical viral immobilization. Furthermore, trivalent peramivir-Fc conjugate (AVC-P3) is synthesised and exhibits stronger antiviral activity than AVC-Z3 in vitro, with much longer half-life in vivo than AVC-Z3, and CD388 with YTE mutation. The in vivo antivirus efficacy of AVC-P3 surpasses other AVCs, baloxavir, and CD388 in H1N1-, H3N2-, H5N1-, and influenza B-infection mice models. Together, our findings define ligand valency as a determinant of antiviral mechanism.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the mechanisms by which Fc conjugation reshapes small-molecule antiviral function, particularly in the context of influenza A and B viruses. The background highlights the need to understand how long-acting drug-Fc conjugates, such as CD388, function against influenza, despite their potential.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study established a multivalent antiviral conjugates (AVCs) platform using click chemistry to enable flexible combination of valencies and conjugated drugs. It focused on avian influenza A viruses and evaluated the antiviral activity of trivalent zanamivir-Fc conjugates (AVC-Z3) and trivalent peramivir-Fc conjugates (AVC-P3) in vitro and in vivo.
analysis.methods: The researchers used click chemistry to create multivalent antiviral conjugates, including mono-, di-, and trivalent versions of zanamivir and peramivir conjugated with Fc. They assessed antiviral activity through in vitro and in vivo experiments, comparing the efficacy of these conjugates against other antivirals and evaluating their half-life in vivo.
analysis.main_results: Trivalent zanamivir-Fc conjugates (AVC-Z3) showed higher antiviral activity than lower-valent AVCs. Trivalent peramivir-Fc conjugates (AVC-P3) exhibited stronger antiviral activity than AVC-Z3 in vitro and had a much longer half-life in vivo compared to AVC-Z3 and CD388 with YTE mutation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that ligand valency determines the antiviral mechanism, shifting from neuraminidase suppression to physical viral immobilization through cross-linking. This represents a novel approach to antiviral therapy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the development of more effective antiviral strategies for avian influenza A viruses, potentially improving surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment options for zoonotic influenza infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro and in vivo experiments with avian influenza models, and the evidence is based on a single model system. The findings are supported by direct experimental results, indicating moderate confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the antiviral mechanisms of multivalent drug-Fc conjugates against avian influenza A viruses. The researchers developed a platform using click chemistry to create mono-, di-, and trivalent antiviral conjugates (AVCs) with zanamivir and peramivir. They found that trivalent zanamivir-Fc conjugates (AVC-Z3) and trivalent peramivir-Fc conjugates (AVC-P3) showed enhanced antiviral activity compared to lower-valent versions. AVC-P3 demonstrated stronger activity in vitro and a longer half-life in vivo than AVC-Z3 and CD388 with YTE mutation. The study suggests that ligand valency influences antiviral mechanisms, shifting from neuraminidase suppression to physical viral immobilization. These findings may inform the development of more effective antiviral strategies for avian influenza, particularly in zoonotic contexts. However, the evidence is based on a limited set of in vitro and in vivo models, which may affect generalizability.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究利用点击化学建立了多价 抗病毒药物 缀合物 (AVC) 平台,以实现化合价和缀合药物的灵活组合。它专注于 禽流感 A 病毒,并评估了三价扎那米韦-Fc 缀合物 (AVC-Z3) 和三价帕拉米韦-Fc 缀合物 (AVC-P3) 的体外和体内 抗病毒药物 活性。

elements_zh.main_results: 三价扎那米韦-Fc 缀合物 (AVC-Z3) 表现出比较低价 AVC 更高的 抗病毒药物 活性。三价帕拉米韦-Fc 缀合物 (AVC-P3) 在体外表现出比 AVC-Z3 更强的 抗病毒药物 活性,与 YTE 突变 的 AVC-Z3 和 CD388 相比,在体内具有更长的半衰期。

abstract_zh: 摘要:长效药物-Fc 结合物​​ (CD388) 已成为抗甲型和乙型流感病毒的新型 抗病毒药物,但 Fc 结合如何重塑小分子功能的机制仍不清楚。在这里,我们通过点击化学建立了一个可编程多价 抗病毒药物 缀合物(AVC)平台,该平台能够灵活组合化合价和缀合药物,从而允许系统地询问化合价依赖性 抗病毒药物 机制。以扎那米韦为模型,单价、二价和三价扎那米韦与 Fc 缀合,其中三价扎那米韦-Fc 缀合物 (AVC-Z3) 表现出比低价 AVC 更高的活性。AVC-Z3 诱导病毒颗粒间聚集,从而将病毒进入的阻断与病毒释放的限制结合起来。这种交联介导的双阶段抑制代表了从神经氨酸酶抑制到物理病毒固定的机制转变。此外,合成了三价帕拉米韦-Fc缀合物(AVC-P3),并在体外表现出比AVC-Z3更强的抗病毒药物活性,体内半衰期比AVC-Z3和YTE 突变的CD388长得多。在 H1N1、H3N2、H5N1 和乙型流感感染小鼠模型中,AVC-P3 的体内抗病毒功效超过其他 AVC、巴洛沙韦和 CD388。总之,我们的研究结果将配体价态定义为 抗病毒药物 机制的决定因素。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在研究 Fc 结合重塑小分子 抗病毒药物 功能的机制,特别是在甲型和乙型流感病毒的背景下。这一背景凸显了了解长效药物-Fc 缀合物(例如 CD388)如何发挥抗流感作用的必要性,尽管它们具有潜力。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究利用点击化学建立了多价 抗病毒药物 缀合物 (AVC) 平台,以实现化合价和缀合药物的灵活组合。它专注于 禽流感 A 病毒,并评估了三价扎那米韦-Fc 缀合物 (AVC-Z3) 和三价帕拉米韦-Fc 缀合物 (AVC-P3) 的体外和体内 抗病毒药物 活性。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员使用点击化学创建了多价 抗病毒药物 缀合物,包括与 Fc 缀合的扎那米韦和帕拉米韦的单价、二价和三价版本。他们通过体外和体内实验评估了 抗病毒药物 的活性,将这些缀合物与其他 抗病毒药物 的功效进行比较,并评估其体内半衰期。
analysis_zh.main_results: 三价扎那米韦-Fc 缀合物 (AVC-Z3) 表现出比较低价 AVC 更高的 抗病毒药物 活性。三价帕拉米韦-Fc 缀合物 (AVC-P3) 在体外表现出比 AVC-Z3 更强的 抗病毒药物 活性,与 YTE 突变 的 AVC-Z3 和 CD388 相比,在体内具有更长的半衰期。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,配体价决定了 抗病毒药物 机制,从神经氨酸酶抑制转变为通过交联进行物理病毒固定。这代表了 抗病毒药物 治疗的一种新方法。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为针对 禽流感 A 病毒开发更有效的 抗病毒药物 策略提供了见解,可能改善人畜共患流感感染的 监测、诊断 和 治疗 选择。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于 禽流感 模型的体外和体内实验,证据基于单一模型系统。这些发现得到了直接实验结果的支持,表明有一定的信心。

title: Adjuvanted Influenza Vaccines Versus Other Influenza Vaccines in Adults Aged ≥60 Years: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Relative Effectiveness for Preventing Influenza-Related Hospitalization
abstract: Background/Objectives: Seasonal influenza vaccines have been developed to reduce the risk of severe complications in older adults, who are at increased risk of influenza-related morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to synthesize the available evidence on the comparative effectiveness of MF59-adjuvanted versus high-dose and non-adjuvanted influenza vaccines in preventing hospitalization/ED access. Methods: A systematic literature review of observational and pragmatic studies was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines. Eligibility was set at ≥60 years. Results: Initially, 1556 records were identified for screening by title and abstract. After removing duplicates (n = 378), 1122 were judged ineligible; 56 records were screened for full-text evaluation. The reconciled dataset contained 13 publications for ADJ versus HD (12 with overall-population estimates and one with risk-stratum estimates) and eight for ADJ versus SD; two publications contributed to both comparisons. All included studies concerned adults aged ≥65 years. In the exploratory overall displays, including explicitly identified broader outcomes, exploratory summaries across adjusted ratio measures were 0.977 (95% normal-theory CI 0.946 to 1.010) for MF59-adjuvanted versus high-dose vaccines (12 publications, 12 estimates; I2 = 75.8%; 95% prediction interval 0.891 to 1.072) and 0.818 (95% normal-theory CI 0.783 to 0.855) versus standard-dose vaccines (eight publications, eight estimates; I2 = 41.6%; 95% prediction interval 0.758 to 0.883; Hartung–Knapp CI 0.766 to 0.875). Conclusions: The exploratory synthesis did not show a clear difference between MF59-adjuvanted and high-dose vaccines. The average favored adjuvanted over standard-dose vaccines, but sensitivity to outcome selection, heterogeneity estimation and potentially overlapping populations limits interpretation.

title: Breaking the channel barrier: same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy enables seven-target respiratory virus detection on a six-channel PCR platform within 20 minutes.
abstract: BACKGROUND Respiratory pathogens with overlapping symptoms-including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, H5/H7/H10 avian influenza, and RSV-co-circulate and co-infect, demanding rapid multiplex screening at points of care. Conventional multiplex real-time PCR is constrained by hardware channel capacity (≤6), making it difficult to detect seven targets while distinguishing influenza A and B in a single tube. This work addresses the contradiction between high-order multiplexing and limited fluorescence channels without sacrificing speed or sensitivity. RESULTS We developed a six-channel ultra-fast PCR platform detecting seven respiratory viruses in a single tube within 20 min, using a same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy. Influenza A and B share the FAM channel yet generate distinct melting peaks (∼12 °C difference, 84.8 °C vs. 72.3 °C), enabling accurate typing via melting curve analysis. Primers, probes, and enzymes are pre-embedded as lyophilized beads in sealed cartridges for fully automated sample-to-result operation. The assay achieved 100% detection at 5 copies/test for all targets, linearity (R2 > 0.95) across 5-105 copies/test, 90-110% efficiencies, and no cross-reactivity against 39 non-target pathogens. Cartridges remained stable for 12 months at 25 °C. Validation on 271 clinical specimens showed 100% agreement with sequencing-verified single-plex qPCR. SIGNIFICANCE AND NOVELTY This work provides the first integration of melting-curve-based same-channel multiplexing with lyophilized cartridge technology on an ultra-fast PCR platform. By overcoming channel limitations while maintaining speed and sensitivity, the system offers a practical, field-deployable screening tool for decentralized respiratory pathogen detection in resource-limited settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a novel six-channel PCR platform that enables the detection of seven respiratory viruses, including avian influenza A viruses, in a single tube within 20 minutes. The platform uses a same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy to distinguish between influenza A and B, which share the same fluorescent channel. The assay demonstrated 100% detection at 5 copies per test, linearity across a wide range of copy numbers, and no cross-reactivity with non-target pathogens. The system is designed for fully automated operation using lyophilized beads, making it suitable for decentralized use in resource-limited settings. The work represents the first integration of melting-curve-based same-channel multiplexing with lyophilized cartridge technology on an ultra-fast PCR platform. The study's results are based on validation using 271 clinical specimens, showing 100% agreement with sequencing-verified single-plex qPCR. The findings suggest that this platform could improve rapid and accurate respiratory virus detection at points of care, particularly for avian influenza A viruses.

title_zh: 打破通道障碍:同荧光、不同Tm探针策略可在20分钟内在六通道PCR平台上实现七靶标呼吸道病毒检测。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND Respiratory pathogens with overlapping symptoms-including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, H5/H7/H10 avian influenza, and RSV-co-circulate and co-infect, demanding rapid multiplex screening at points of care. Conventional multiplex real-time PCR is constrained by hardware channel capacity (≤6), making it difficult to detect seven targets while distinguishing influenza A and B in a single tube. This work addresses the contradiction between high-order multiplexing and limited fluorescence channels without sacrificing speed or sensitivity. RESULTS We developed a six-channel ultra-fast PCR platform detecting seven respiratory viruses in a single tube within 20 min, using a same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy. Influenza A and B share the FAM channel yet generate distinct melting peaks (∼12 °C difference, 84.8 °C vs. 72.3 °C), enabling accurate typing via melting curve analysis. Primers, probes, and enzymes are pre-embedded as lyophilized beads in sealed cartridges for fully automated sample-to-result operation. The assay achieved 100% detection at 5 copies/test for all targets, linearity (R2 > 0.95) across 5-105 copies/test, 90-110% efficiencies, and no cross-reactivity against 39 non-target pathogens. Cartridges remained stable for 12 months at 25 °C. Validation on 271 clinical specimens showed 100% agreement with sequencing-verified single-plex qPCR. SIGNIFICANCE AND NOVELTY This work provides the first integration of melting-curve-based same-channel multiplexing with lyophilized cartridge technology on an ultra-fast PCR platform. By overcoming channel limitations while maintaining speed and sensitivity, the system offers a practical, field-deployable screening tool for decentralized respiratory pathogen detection in resource-limited settings.
abstract_zh: 背景 具有重叠症状的呼吸道病原体(包括 SARS-CoV-2、甲型/乙型流感、H5/H7/H10 禽流感 和 RSV)共同循环和共同感染,需要在护理点进行快速多重筛查。传统多重实时PCR受硬件通道容量(≤6)的限制,难以在单管中检测​​7个靶标并区分甲型和乙型流感。这项工作在不牺牲速度或灵敏度的情况下解决了高阶多重和有限荧光通道之间的矛盾。结果我们开发了一个六通道超快速 PCR 平台,使用相同荧光、不同 Tm 探针策略,可在 20 分钟内检测单管中的七种呼吸道病毒。甲型流感和乙型流感共享 FAM 通道,但会产生不同的熔解峰(~12 °C 差异,84.8 °C 与 72.3 °C),从而可以通过熔解曲线分析进行准确分型。引物、探针和酶以冻干珠的形式预先嵌入密封盒中,以实现全自动样品到结果操作。该检测在 5 个拷贝/测试中对所有目标实现了 100% 检测,在 5-105 个拷贝/测试中实现了线性 (R2 > 0.95),效率为 90-110%,并且与 39 种非目标病原体没有交叉反应。墨盒在 25 °C 下可保持稳定 12 个月。对 271 个临床样本的验证显示与测序验证的单重 qPCR 100% 一致。意义和新颖性 这项工作首次将基于熔解曲线的同通道多重技术与冻干柱技术在超快速 PCR 平台上集成。通过克服通道限制,同时保持速度和灵敏度,该系统提供了一种实用的、可现场部署的筛查工具,用于在资源有限的环境中进行分散的呼吸道病原体检测。

title: Structural and functional stability of lyophilized nonencapsulated mRNA synthesized in vitro during long-term storage
abstract: The low physicochemical stability of mRNA and the dependence of current mRNA vaccines on the successful encapsulation into lipid nanoparticles and adherence to mandatory cold chain requirements limit their storage and transportation. A promising approach is the lyophilization of nonencapsulated mRNA with its subsequent delivery by jet injection. However, the preservation of its structure and functional activity during long-term storage has been insufficiently studied. To evaluate the structural and functional stability of lyophilized nonencapsulated mRNA during long-term storage and its immunogenicity as a component of a trivalent mRNA vaccine against seasonal influenza administered to mice by jet injection. MATERIALS AND METHODS. mRNA encoding green fluorescent protein (GFP) was lyophilized with various cryoprotectants and stored at −20, 4, and 20 °C. Its functional activity was determined by GFP expression after transfection of HEK293 cells, and its integrity was analyzed by microchip electrophoresis. The immunogenicity of the lyophilized and nonlyophilized mRNA-Vector-Flu vaccine was evaluated in female inbred BALB/c mice after two jet immunizations by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) assay, virus neutralization assay, and interferon gamma (IFN-γ) enzyme-linked immunospot (ELISpot) assay. Based on the results of a preliminary screening, a 10% trehalose formulation was selected for further studies because it preserved the functional activity of GFP mRNA at the level closest to that of the control preparation. The lyophilized GFP mRNA retained its functional activity after 12 months of storage at all tested temperatures; no statistically significant differences were found compared with the mRNA synthesized immediately before use ( p >0.05). The major mRNA fraction was preserved, although minor fractions of partially degraded mRNA were detected after 6–12 months, particularly at 20 °C. After 3 months of storage of the vaccine at 4 °C, the geometric mean antibody titers against hemagglutinin subtype 1 (H1), hemagglutinin subtype 3 (H3), and influenza B hemagglutinin (HB) were 1:382,000, 1:628,000, and 1:273,000, respectively, compared with 1:710,000, 1:628,000, and 1:328,000 in the nonlyophilized vaccine group. HAI titers were 1:37–1:80, virus-neutralizing antibody titers were 1:50–1:90; and the numbers of IFN-γ-secreting cells were 440 and 500 spot-forming cells (SFC) per 1×10 6 splenocytes. No significant between-group differences were identified. Lyophilization with 10% trehalose preserved the functional activity of nonencapsulated mRNA for 12 months despite signs of partial degradation at 20 °C. After 3 months of storage at 4 °C, the trivalent vaccine retained its ability to induce humoral and T-cell immune responses in mice. These findings support the potential of combining lyophilization and jet injection for the development of stable mRNA vaccines.

full_text: AbstractCattle now occupy two epidemiologically distinct influenza interfaces. This Mini Review comparatively synthesizes epidemiological, pathological, experimental-transmission, genomic, and surveillance evidence for highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) and influenza D virus (IDV), asking how source ecology, tissue tropism, shedding, transmission, persistence, and zoonotic evidence differ between the two viruses. Genetically distinct H5N1 viruses have spilled over repeatedly from wild birds into United States dairy cattle. In lactating cows, infection is prominent in mammary alveolar epithelium and produces high titers of infectious virus in raw milk; inter-herd cattle movements have disseminated genotype B3.13 through dairy production networks. On affected farms, viral RNA has been detected in milk and respiratory specimens; infectious virus is recovered consistently from raw milk and mammary tissues but only sporadically from respiratory or environmental samples such as milking-parlour air and wastewater. These findings identify exposure settings but do not resolve the dominant natural cow-to-cow transmission route or how the virus reaches the mammary gland. Occupational infections have occurred, but sustained cattle adaptation or long-term reservoir status has not been demonstrated. In contrast, IDV is a cattle-adapted respiratory virus maintained through direct contact and short-range airborne transmission, with interlineage reassortment among IDV genome segments and frequent association with bovine respiratory disease complex (BRDC), although an independent causal role in BRDC remains unproven. Human seroreactivity and efficient replication in human airway models indicate exposure and biological compatibility, but not confirmed productive human infection or onward transmission. These contrasts support event-triggered, milk-centered investigation for H5N1 and longitudinal respiratory and genomic surveillance for IDV, built on shared One Health diagnostic, sequencing, epidemiological, and occupational-health infrastructure.Keywords: bovine respiratory disease complex, cattle, cross-species transmission, highly pathogenic avian influenza a(H5N1), influenza D virus, mammary tropism, one health surveillance 6.DiscussionAlthough both viruses infect cattle, their assessment requires different risk frameworks. Epidemiological consequences depend on the principal replication site and its relationship to production. In H5N1-infected dairy cows, mammary infection links viral shedding to milk production and milking practices. High-titer shedding in milk creates a direct exposure pathway; animal movements facilitate dissemination, while occupational contact creates opportunities for human exposure. IDV lacks this production-linked route; instead, it is maintained by respiratory transmission and interacts with other pathogens within the polymicrobial setting of BRDC. The most informative samples, genomic priorities, and response thresholds therefore differ.The principal uncertainties differ between the two viruses. For H5N1, the natural portal of entry, the relative contributions of milking-associated, respiratory, and environmental transmission, and whether cattle constitute a long-term reservoir remain unresolved. For IDV, respiratory replication and cattle-to-cattle transmission are established, but its independent contribution to naturally occurring BRDC remains uncertain, as does the clinical significance of human exposure signals. Resolving these questions will require studies that integrate viral kinetics with tissue lesions, co-pathogen dynamics, animal-movement histories, clinical outcomes, and transmission phenotypes.The supporting evidence is asymmetric in scope and design. H5N1 evidence derives mainly from intensively investigated outbreaks in lactating United States dairy cattle and a few experiments; extrapolation to non-lactating cattle, beef cattle, calves, and other production systems remains uncertain. IDV studies span more regions and years but often use cross-sectional PCR or serology, heterogeneous sampling, and incomplete genomic data. These differences preclude simple comparisons of prevalence, transmission efficiency, pathogenicity, or zoonotic risk. Preparedness should therefore reflect virus-specific replication sites and production systems rather than host species alone. 1.IntroductionInfluenza A virus ecology is commonly framed around wild aquatic birds as the principal natural reservoir, with poultry, swine, and humans occupying different host roles in amplification, reassortment, adaptation, and disease emergence (Krammer et al., 2018). Cattle received little attention because sustained influenza A virus circulation had not been documented in bovine populations. In 2024, clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) [HPAI A(H5N1)] was confirmed in United States dairy cattle (Caserta et al., 2024), and genomic analysis traced spread through interconnected dairy production networks (Nguyen et al., 2025). A joint assessment by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), World Health Organization (WHO), and World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH), based on data available through 1 March 2026, documented several independent spillovers from wild birds into cattle, demonstrating that multiple viral genotypes can infect this host (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations et al., 2026).The emergence of H5N1 in dairy cattle established a production-linked influenza interface centered on lactation, milking, and cattle movement. Field and experimental studies documented mammary infection, high virus titers in milk, mastitis, abnormal milk, and production loss (Caserta et al., 2024; Baker et al., 2025; Peña-Mosca et al., 2025). Movement of infected cattle facilitated long-distance dissemination (Nguyen et al., 2025), whereas genetically distinct spillovers from wild birds created new points of entry (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations et al., 2026). Thus, raw milk and milking procedures are central exposure settings, cattle movement links herds, and contaminated equipment, aerosols, wastewater, cross-species contact, and occupational contact define additional exposure pathways whose contributions to natural transmission remain unresolved.Influenza D virus (IDV) follows a different ecological pattern. First isolated from a pig with respiratory disease (Hause et al., 2013), it was later established as a distinct orthomyxovirus with cattle as its principal maintenance host (Hause et al., 2014). Experimental studies in calves demonstrated direct-contact (Ferguson et al., 2016) and short-range airborne transmission (Salem et al., 2019). Case-control (Ng et al., 2015) and cohort (Nissly et al., 2020) studies associate IDV with bovine respiratory disease complex (BRDC) without establishing independent or dominant causation. Whole-genome studies document diversification and geographic structure (Limaye et al., 2024), interlineage reassortment among IDV genome segments (Collin et al., 2015), and regional persistence (Li H. et al., 2026), favoring longitudinal surveillance over outbreak-limited investigation.The two viruses differ most clearly in their principal replication sites. Mammary replication links H5N1 to milk and dairy production networks, whereas respiratory replication links IDV to enzootic circulation and BRDC. We therefore compare shedding, transmission, disease context, evolutionary dynamics, and surveillance across these compartments, while distinguishing occupational exposure signals from evidence of productive human infection or onward transmission. 2.Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in dairy cattle: emergence, mammary infection, and unresolved transmission routesThe United States cattle epizootic was initially dominated by genotype B3.13. Phylogenetic and epidemiological analysis support a single wild-bird-to-bovine spillover followed by extensive cattle-associated, movement-linked spread (Nguyen et al., 2025). Genotype D1.1 detections in Nevada and Arizona represented two additional independent spillovers from wild birds, each with limited cattle transmission (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations et al., 2026). Repeated entry and sustained circulation are therefore separate processes. Unresolved questions are how often wild-bird-derived H5N1 crosses into cattle, which changes arise after spillover, and which routes sustain transmission. Extensive cattle-associated spread alone does not establish long-term reservoir status.After introduction, the distinctive pathological feature in lactating cows is mammary infection. Field investigations detected abundant viral RNA and infectious virus in milk, epithelial necrosis, and H5N1 antigen by immunohistochemistry in mammary alveolar epithelial cells (Caserta et al., 2024). Intramammary inoculation reproduced severe mastitis, abnormal milk, reduced production, and high-titer milk shedding (Baker et al., 2025). In contrast, oronasal inoculation of calves produced moderate upper-respiratory replication and nasal shedding, without detected transmission to sentinels (Halwe et al., 2025). Because these experiments differed in age, lactation status, target tissue, and inoculation route, they establish mammary tropism but do not identify the natural entry route.Transmission evidence remains less definitive. Low-dose intramammary challenge caused robust infection and high-titer shedding in milk, but transmission to sentinel cows was not detected despite repeated exposure to contaminated milking equipment and close contact. Respiratory and oral exposures were also less efficient than intramammary inoculation at establishing productive infection under the tested conditions (Lee et al., 2026). Across 14 California dairy farms, infectious virus was recovered from milking-parlour air on three farms and from wastewater on one farm; viral RNA was also detected in exhaled breath and milk from cows without overt clinical signs (Campbell et al., 2026). The persistent, spatially heterogeneous distribution of positive udder quarters suggested that shared milking equipment was unlikely to be the sole route. Collectively, these observations identify plausible exposure settings but do not resolve the natural portal of entry or the route by which the virus reaches the mammary gland.Mechanistic studies have examined why mammary tissue is permissive. Plant lectins and haemagglutinin probes identified glycans compatible with contemporary avian H5 binding, but gave discordant signals for putative human-type receptors; lectin staining cannot establish functional receptor use (Kristensen et al., 2024; Rios Carrasco et al., 2024). Glycan binding also cannot explain route-specific infection or farm transmission. A bovine clade 2.3.4.4b isolate replicated in mammary and airway organoids without demonstrating respiratory transmission in vivo (Li C. et al., 2026). Intramammary challenge elicited compartmentalized cytokine responses, systemic myeloid remodeling, lymphocyte activation, and increased H5- and N1-specific antibody titers (Singh et al., 2026). Protease availability, local innate immunity, tissue physiology, dose, and lactation stage may also contribute.The consequences of mammary infection extend from production loss to cross-species exposure. In one affected herd, about one fifth of adult cows developed clinical disease, and average milk production per affected cow was estimated to be 901 kg lower than expected during the 60 days after diagnosis (Peña-Mosca et al., 2025). Because this estimate comes from a single herd, it should not be extrapolated across management systems. Raw milk or colostrum from infected cows can also expose other species: farm cats fed these products developed fatal systemic and neurological disease, and closely related viruses were found in cattle and cats on the same premises (Burrough et al., 2024).For people, the clearest evidence is occupational spillover. The first recognized infection involved a Texas dairy worker who developed conjunctivitis after exposure to affected cattle (Uyeki et al., 2024). Additional infections were later identified among dairy workers, who usually presented with conjunctivitis or mild respiratory illness (Garg et al., 2025). These cases do not demonstrate sustained human-to-human transmission. The May 2026 FAO/WHO/WOAH assessment rated the global risk to the general population as low and the risk to occupationally or frequently exposed people as low to moderate, depending on local epidemiology and protective measures (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations et al., 2026). A WHO update covering reports available through 7 July 2026 likewise found no sustained human-to-human transmission of A(H5) viruses (World Health Organization, 2026). Validated commercial pasteurization conditions effectively inactivate H5N1, whereas raw milk from infected cattle may expose people and animals to infectious virus (United States Food and Drug Administration, 2026).At the viral level, replication in cattle creates a new selective environment for H5N1. Early in the outbreak, polymerase substitutions including PB2 M631L and PA K497R became enriched among cattle-associated viruses and were shown to increase polymerase activity in bovine cells and enhance viral replication in mammary tissue models (Dholakia et al., 2026). However, these substitutions have not been shown to confer efficient bovine respiratory or airborne transmission, and their detection alone is insufficient to infer pandemic potential (Dholakia et al., 2026; Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations et al., 2026). Substitutions that recur or increase in frequency should be evaluated phenotypically in relevant bovine and other mammalian models. 3.Influenza D virus in cattle: enzootic respiratory circulation, BRDC, and evolutionIDV was first isolated in 2011 from a pig with respiratory disease and described as influenza C-like (Hause et al., 2013). Subsequent work established IDV as a distinct orthomyxovirus and identified cattle as its principal maintenance host, based partly on substantially higher seroprevalence in cattle than in swine (Hause et al., 2014). Surveillance has since documented broad but uneven circulation in bovine populations (Collin et al., 2015; Limaye et al., 2024; Li H. et al., 2026).In experimentally infected cattle, IDV replicates in the upper and lower airways, causes mild clinical signs and tracheal lesions, and transmits to direct-contact animals (Ferguson et al., 2016). In another experiment, sentinel calves housed 3 m from aerosol-inoculated animals became infected despite the absence of direct or fomite contact, supporting short-range airborne transmission (Salem et al., 2019). Together, these experiments support direct-contact and short-range airborne transmission. Transport and commingling may amplify transmission under field conditions, although their contributions to the long-term maintenance of IDV in cattle populations have not been quantified.IDV is transmissible among cattle, but its independent role in BRDC remains uncertain. A metagenomic case-control study detected IDV more often in cattle with severe respiratory disease than in matched controls (Ng et al., 2015). A later cohort linked higher IDV loads and a greater burden of viral coinfection with clinical disease (Nissly et al., 2020). BRDC is nevertheless multifactorial and is shaped by transport stress, crowding, host immune status, bacterial colonization, management practices, and multiple viral infections. An IDV-positive RT-qPCR result confirms the presence of viral RNA in the tested respiratory specimen but does not by itself distinguish active infection from transient carriage or establish that IDV caused the clinical syndrome.Coinfection experiments provide evidence of disease enhancement. Calves infected with both IDV and Mycoplasma bovis developed earlier and more severe disease than calves given either agent alone, and IDV promoted M. bovis colonization of the lower respiratory tract (Lion et al., 2021). These findings support a contributory role for IDV within the BRDC pathogen network, although the magnitude of that contribution remains uncertain. Prospective studies should relate viral kinetics to airway lesions, bacterial colonization of the lower respiratory tract, host responses, and clinical outcomes.Enzootic circulation provides repeated opportunities for diversification. Early work identified cocirculating D/OK and D/660 lineages and interlineage reassortment among the seven IDV genome segments (Collin et al., 2015). Subsequent whole-genome analysis revealed further diversification, geographic structure, and additional interlineage reassortment (Limaye et al., 2024). In Northeast China, D/Yamagata/2019-lineage viruses were detected only sporadically, yet phylogenetic continuity indicated ongoing circulation (Li H. et al., 2026). full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractCattle now occupy two epidemiologically distinct influenza interfaces. This Mini Review comparatively synthesizes epidemiological, pathological, experimental-transmission, genomic, and surveillance evidence for highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) and influenza D virus (IDV), asking how source ecology, tissue tropism, shedding, transmission, persistence, and zoonotic evidence differ between the two viruses. Genetically distinct H5N1 viruses have spilled over repeatedly from wild birds into United States dairy cattle. In lactating cows, infection is prominent in mammary alveolar epithelium and produces high titers of infectious virus in raw milk; inter-herd cattle movements have disseminated genotype B3.13 through dairy production networks. On affected farms, viral RNA has been detected in milk and respiratory specimens; infectious virus is recovered consistently from raw milk and mammary tissues but only sporadically from respiratory or environmental samples such as milking-parlour air and wastewater. These findings identify exposure settings but do not resolve the dominant natural cow-to-cow transmission route or how the virus reaches the mammary gland. Occupational infections have occurred, but sustained cattle adaptation or long-term reservoir status has not been demonstrated. In contrast, IDV is a cattle-adapted respiratory virus maintained through direct contact and short-range airborne transmission, with interlineage reassortment among IDV genome segments and frequent association with bovine respiratory disease complex (BRDC), although an independent causal role in BRDC remains unproven. Human seroreactivity and efficient replication in human airway models indicate exposure and biological compatibility, but not confirmed productive human infection or onward transmission. These contrasts support event-triggered, milk-centered investigation for H5N1 and longitudinal respiratory and genomic surveillance for IDV, built on shared One Health diagnostic, sequencing, epidemiological, and occupational-health infrastructure.Keywords: bovine respiratory disease complex, cattle, cross-species transmission, highly pathogenic avian influenza a(H5N1), influenza D virus, mammary tropism, one health surveillance
full_text_sections.discussion: 6.DiscussionAlthough both viruses infect cattle, their assessment requires different risk frameworks. Epidemiological consequences depend on the principal replication site and its relationship to production. In H5N1-infected dairy cows, mammary infection links viral shedding to milk production and milking practices. High-titer shedding in milk creates a direct exposure pathway; animal movements facilitate dissemination, while occupational contact creates opportunities for human exposure. IDV lacks this production-linked route; instead, it is maintained by respiratory transmission and interacts with other pathogens within the polymicrobial setting of BRDC. The most informative samples, genomic priorities, and response thresholds therefore differ.The principal uncertainties differ between the two viruses. For H5N1, the natural portal of entry, the relative contributions of milking-associated, respiratory, and environmental transmission, and whether cattle constitute a long-term reservoir remain unresolved. For IDV, respiratory replication and cattle-to-cattle transmission are established, but its independent contribution to naturally occurring BRDC remains uncertain, as does the clinical significance of human exposure signals. Resolving these questions will require studies that integrate viral kinetics with tissue lesions, co-pathogen dynamics, animal-movement histories, clinical outcomes, and transmission phenotypes.The supporting evidence is asymmetric in scope and design. H5N1 evidence derives mainly from intensively investigated outbreaks in lactating United States dairy cattle and a few experiments; extrapolation to non-lactating cattle, beef cattle, calves, and other production systems remains uncertain. IDV studies span more regions and years but often use cross-sectional PCR or serology, heterogeneous sampling, and incomplete genomic data. These differences preclude simple comparisons of prevalence, transmission efficiency, pathogenicity, or zoonotic risk. Preparedness should therefore reflect virus-specific replication sites and production systems rather than host species alone.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how the ecology, tissue tropism, shedding, transmission, persistence, and zoonotic potential of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) and influenza D virus (IDV) differ, with a focus on their distinct interfaces in cattle.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved case-control and cohort studies in dairy cattle, examining the epidemiological and clinical associations of H5N1 and IDV with bovine respiratory disease complex (BRDC) and milk production. It also included metagenomic analyses and longitudinal surveillance across different regions and time periods.
analysis.methods: The study employed metagenomic sequencing, PCR, serology, and experimental transmission studies in calves to investigate shedding, transmission, and disease context. Whole-genome sequencing was emphasized to trace viral movement and reassortment events.
analysis.main_results: Viral RNA was detected in milk and respiratory specimens of H5N1-infected cows, with infectious virus consistently recovered from raw milk and mammary tissues. For IDV, higher viral loads and coinfections were associated with clinical disease, but no independent causal role in BRDC was confirmed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the distinct replication sites and transmission dynamics of H5N1 and IDV, emphasizing the need for virus-specific surveillance strategies and risk frameworks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform targeted surveillance and risk management strategies for H5N1 and IDV, particularly in dairy production systems and respiratory disease contexts, by identifying unique exposure pathways and transmission routes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by the reliance on cross-sectional PCR and serology for IDV, and by unresolved uncertainties regarding the natural portal of entry and transmission routes for H5N1. The confidence is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the distinct interfaces of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) and influenza D virus (IDV) in cattle, emphasizing their different replication sites and transmission dynamics. H5N1 is associated with mammary alveolar epithelium, leading to high viral shedding in milk and dissemination through animal movements. IDV, on the other hand, is a cattle-adapted respiratory virus maintained by direct contact and short-range airborne transmission, often linked to bovine respiratory disease complex (BRDC). The research highlights the need for virus-specific surveillance strategies, as the principal replication sites and production systems influence epidemiological consequences. However, the study has limitations, including reliance on cross-sectional methods for IDV and unresolved uncertainties about H5N1 transmission routes. The findings suggest that preparedness should reflect these differences rather than focusing solely on host species, with moderate confidence in the conclusions due to the nature of the evidence and unresolved questions.

title: Advances and challenges in avian influenza vaccines: From conventional approaches to next-generation strategies
abstract: Background Avian influenza viruses (AIVs), particularly highly pathogenic H5 and H7 viruses, pose major threats to poultry production, food security, international trade, and public health. Vaccination is an important component of AIV control; however, antigenic evolution, incomplete reduction of viral shedding, and challenges associated with large-scale poultry vaccination limit its effectiveness. In addition to conventional vaccines, recombinant and nucleic-acid platforms have emerged in response to rapidly evolving AIVs. Methods Relevant literature on inactivated, live attenuated, recombinant subunit, viral-vector, DNA, mRNA, and virus-like particle vaccines was evaluated. Immune responses, protection, antigenic breadth, viral shedding, delivery, manufacturing, field applicability, and regulatory considerations were analyzed. Results Inactivated vaccines are well-established, safe, scalable, and cost-effective but provide limited cellular and mucosal immunity and require antigenic matching. Live attenuated vaccines can induce broader immunity and facilitate mass vaccination but present biosafety, reassortment, and genetic-stability concerns. Next-generation platforms provide greater antigenic flexibility and opportunities for broader protection. Viral-vector vaccines can induce both humoral and cellular immunity, while recombinant subunit, DNA, mRNA, and VLP vaccines offer rapid redesign and multivalent formulations. However, challenges remain regarding delivery, stability, manufacturing, durability, and field validation. Conclusions No single platform currently meets all requirements for sustainable AIV control. Future strategies should emphasize conserved or mosaic antigens, durable and mucosal immunity, rapid vaccine updating, DIVA compatibility, and scalable delivery. Combining conventional and emerging platforms through prime-boost or multi-platform strategies may provide more flexible and effective control.

analysis.summary_en: This study reviews the current state of avian influenza vaccines, highlighting the limitations of conventional approaches and the potential of next-generation strategies. It identifies inactivated vaccines as safe and scalable but notes their limited immunity and need for antigenic matching. Live attenuated vaccines are discussed for their broader immunity and mass vaccination potential, though they raise biosafety concerns. Next-generation platforms are noted for their antigenic flexibility and opportunities for broader protection. The authors conclude that no single platform currently meets all requirements for sustainable avian influenza control and suggest future strategies should focus on conserved antigens, durable immunity, and scalable delivery. The study emphasizes the importance of combining conventional and emerging platforms through prime-boost or multi-platform strategies to enhance vaccine effectiveness. The evidence is based on a literature review, which provides moderate confidence in the findings.

abstract_zh: 背景 禽流感病毒(AIVs),特别是高致病性H5和H7病毒,对家禽生产、粮食安全、国际贸易和公共卫生构成重大威胁。疫苗接种是AIV控制的重要组成部分;然而,抗原性进化、病毒 shedding 减少不完全以及大规模家禽疫苗接种相关的挑战限制了其有效性。除了传统疫苗,重组和核酸平台已出现以应对快速进化的AIVs。方法 评估了有关灭活、减毒活、重组亚单位、病毒媒介、DNA、mRNA和病毒样颗粒疫苗的相关文献。分析了免疫应答、保护效果、抗原广度、病毒 shedding、递送方式、制造、现场应用和监管考虑。结果 灭活疫苗已建立、安全、可扩展且成本效益高,但其诱导的细胞和黏膜免疫有限,且需要抗原匹配。减毒活疫苗可诱导更广泛的免疫应答,并有助于大规模疫苗接种,但存在生物安全、基因重组和遗传稳定性方面的担忧。下一代平台提供了更大的抗原灵活性和更广泛的保护机会。病毒媒介 疫苗可同时诱导体液和细胞免疫,而重组亚单位、DNA、mRNA和VLP 疫苗则提供了快速重新设计和多价制剂的可能性。然而,关于递送、稳定性、制造、持续性和现场验证仍存在挑战。结论 目前没有一种平台能够满足可持续AIV控制的所有要求。未来策略应强调保守或拼接抗原、持久且黏膜免疫、快速疫苗更新、DIVA兼容性以及可扩展的递送方式。通过加强接种或多种平台策略结合传统和新兴平台,可能提供更灵活和有效的控制手段。

title: H5N1 in Australia: psychology, penguins, and preparedness.
abstract: The Australian Antarctic Division (AAD) has announced it will withdraw all its staff from the remote Macquarie Island in Antarctica in October, 2026, citing the likelihood of psychosocial stress on its staff in the event of witnessing mass animal deaths from an impending outbreak of H5N1 (clade 2.3.4.4b lineage).

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the potential psychosocial impact of an impending H5N1 outbreak on staff working in remote locations, particularly in the context of animal deaths and the need for preparedness.

analysis.methods: The methods involve an administrative decision by the Australian Antarctic Division to assess and mitigate psychosocial risks, without detailed experimental or observational procedures.
analysis.main_results: The main result is the decision to withdraw staff from Macquarie Island in October 2026, citing the likelihood of psychosocial stress from witnessing mass animal deaths associated with an H5N1 outbreak.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of considering psychosocial impacts in public health preparedness for zoonotic outbreaks, particularly in isolated environments where staff well-being is critical.

analysis.summary_en: This study discusses the decision by the Australian Antarctic Division to withdraw staff from Macquarie Island in October 2026, citing the anticipated psychosocial stress from witnessing mass animal deaths linked to an H5N1 outbreak. The research highlights the need for preparedness in remote environments, emphasizing the psychological impact of zoonotic disease events. The study is based on an administrative announcement, which limits the evidence strength to moderate. It contributes to the understanding of how public health threats can influence operational decisions in isolated settings, particularly regarding staff well-being. The findings suggest that psychosocial considerations should be integrated into broader outbreak preparedness strategies. The study does not provide detailed methods or results, relying instead on a policy-based decision. While it raises awareness about the human dimension of zoonotic outbreaks, it lacks empirical data to support broader scientific or public health implications.

analysis_zh.main_results: 主要结果是决定于 2026 年 10 月从麦格理岛撤出工作人员,理由是目睹与 H5N1 暴发 相关的大规模动物死亡可能会造成心理社会压力。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这一决定解释为保护员工心理健康的一项主动措施,强调了将 H5N1 暴发 情景与偏远南极行动中的心理社会准备联系起来的新颖性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,在针对人畜共患病 暴发 的公共卫生准备中考虑心理社会影响的重要性,特别是在员工福祉至关重要的偏远环境中。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该证据基于公告,缺乏详细的实证数据,由于缺乏定量或定性分析,导致信心评估适中。

full_text: AbstractHighly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have undergone an unprecedented expansion of host range since 2021, moving from wild birds and poultry into dairy cattle, domestic cats, and other mammals, with sporadic human infections in Europe and North America (Food and Agriculture Organization et al., 2025a; Rolfes et al., 2025). This expansion is underpinned by well-characterised molecular mechanisms of influenza A virus evolution — antigenic drift, gene segment reassortment, and receptor-binding adaptation — that shape the frequency and direction of cross-species spillover (McDonald et al., 2016; Steel and Lowen, 2017; Man et al., 2026). Norwegian wild-bird and mammalian surveillance data document recurrent incursions of clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, and international risk assessments continue to describe low, but non-zero, human risk concentrated among individuals with close animal contact (World Health Organization, 2025–2026; Ytrehus et al; European Food Safety Authority et al., 2025a). Translating this fast-moving virological and epidemiological evidence into everyday protective behavior for children, adolescents, and families remains an underdeveloped link in pandemic preparedness, compounded by documented gaps in adolescent One Health literacy (Zucca et al., 2021). This mini review synthesizes current literature on the molecular basis of influenza cross-species transmission, the Norwegian epidemiological and One Health governance context, and established child- and family-oriented risk-communication frameworks, to argue that Norway’s community-based public health nurses (helsesykepleiere) — who deliver near-universal, statutorily mandated contact with children and families through the helsestasjon- and skolehelsetjeneste — occupy a distinctive but underused position as One Health communication nodes (Helsedirektoratet, 2021). I outline a practical three-tier framework for translating zoonotic-influenza science into age-appropriate household guidance, critically appraise the feasibility, workload, training, and governance implications of this role, and identify priority gaps for future empirical and implementation research.Keywords: avian influenza, cross-species transmission, H5N1, health literacy, helsesykepleier, nordic public health, one health, pandemic preparedness Supplementary materialThe Supplementary Material for this article can be found online at: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fcimb.2026.1965045/full#supplementary-material Supplementary Materials 9.ConclusionThe molecular mechanisms driving the expanding host range of HPAI A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b are the subject of continuous, increasingly granular scientific characterization, and Norwegian wildlife and veterinary surveillance is generating an increasingly detailed picture of local risk. What remains comparatively underdeveloped is the corresponding public-facing translation infrastructure connecting this evolving evidence base to the households where behavior actually changes. Norway’s helsesykepleiere, by virtue of their statutory mandate and near-universal, longitudinal reach into families with children, constitute an existing but underused resource for this translation task — one consistent with, and potentially strengthening, Norway’s own stated One Health governance ambitions (Norwegian Ministry of Health and Care Services; BeReady4Pandemics, 2025). Realizing this potential will require deliberate interdisciplinary collaboration between infection-prevention and virology research groups and the school health service, together with the evaluation research needed to ensure that any resulting communication genuinely improves family-level understanding and protective behavior, rather than simply adding to an already crowded preventive-health agenda. Realizing this potential is conditional on the workload, training, and governance safeguards above being resourced, not assumed cost-free. 1.IntroductionInfluenza A viruses remain among the most consequential zoonotic pathogens of the past century, with all major human pandemics traced to animal reservoirs, most often through reassortment of segmented viral genomes in avian or swine intermediate hosts (de Silva et al., 2012; Steel and Lowen, 2017). Since 2021, however, the epidemiology of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b has departed markedly from this historical pattern. Rather than remaining largely confined to wild birds and commercial poultry, clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have spread into an unprecedented range of mammalian species, including foxes, seals, mink, domestic cats, and, since March 2024, dairy cattle in the United States (Food and Agriculture Organization et al., 2025a; Kamel et al., 2025). Sporadic human infections have followed this mammalian expansion, and while sustained human-to-human transmission has not been documented, international risk assessments describe a dynamic and evolving situation that warrants continued vigilance (World Health Organization, 2025–2026; Rolfes et al., 2025).This shift has practical consequences that extend well beyond veterinary and occupational medicine. Families that keep backyard poultry, own cats fed raw-food diets, or live near wild-bird habitats are now plausibly exposed populations, not merely bystanders to a distant agricultural problem (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 2025a; Vaughan et al., 2026). Yet the substantial and rapidly evolving virological literature on cross-species transmission mechanisms is rarely translated into a form that reaches children, adolescents, and parents at the point where behavior change actually occurs — in the home, the farmyard, or the veterinary clinic waiting room. In Norway, one existing but underused channel for this translation is the corps of community-based public health nurses (helsesykepleiere), who deliver statutorily mandated, near-universal contact with children and families through the child and youth health centers and school health service (Helsedirektoratet, 2021). This mini review synthesizes current literature on (i) the molecular mechanisms underlying influenza A virus cross-species transmission, (ii) the global and Norwegian epidemiological landscape, (iii) Norwegian One Health governance and pandemic-preparedness structures, and (iv) established risk-communication and health-literacy frameworks for children and families, in order to outline a practical framework through which public health nurses can function as One Health communication nodes.Evidence for this mini review was identified through structured searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for English-language literature published between January 2020 and August 2026, using combinations of the terms ‘H5N1’, ‘avian influenza’, ‘clade 2.3.4.4b’, ‘cross-species transmission’, ‘reassortment’, ‘One Health’, ‘risk communication’, ‘health literacy’, ‘helsesykepleier’, and ‘public health nursing’, supplemented by hand-searched reference lists and direct searches of institutional sources (FHI, Norwegian Veterinary Institute, Mattilsynet, WHO, EFSA, and CDC) for current risk assessments and guidance. Given the breadth of the topic and the mini review format, this is a narrative rather than a systematic review, and no formal quality-appraisal tool was applied. The specific search strings and retrieval steps are documented in Supplementary Search Record S1. 2.Molecular evolution and mechanisms of cross-species transmissionInfluenza A viruses possess a genome of eight discrete, single-stranded, negative-sense RNA segments, a structural feature that permits two distinct evolutionary pathways (McDonald et al., 2016). The first, antigenic drift, results from the gradual accumulation of point mutations introduced by the error-prone viral RNA polymerase during replication. The second, and epidemiologically more consequential for cross-species jumps, is reassortment: when two distinct influenza A viruses co-infect the same host cell, progeny virions can package a novel combination of the eight parental segments, generating genetically — and potentially phenotypically — distinct viruses in a single replication cycle (Steel and Lowen, 2017; Selective genome packaging mechanisms of influenza A viruses, 2021). Reassortment between avian, swine, and human lineages produced the reassortant strains responsible for the 1957, 1968, and 2009 pandemics, historically via swine acting as a permissive co-infection host, or ‘mixing vessel’ (de Silva et al., 2012).A second determinant of host range is the receptor-binding specificity of the viral hemagglutinin protein. Avian-adapted viruses preferentially bind α2,3-linked sialic acid receptors predominant in the avian gut and respiratory tract, whereas mammalian-adapted viruses, including human seasonal strains, preferentially bind α2,6-linked receptors characteristic of the upper mammalian respiratory tract. Single amino acid substitutions in the hemagglutinin receptor-binding site, together with adaptive changes in the viral polymerase complex, can shift this binding preference and materially increase a virus’s capacity to infect and transmit within a new mammalian host (Man et al., 2026). Among these changes, PB2 substitutions such as E627K and D701N improve polymerase activity at mammalian upper-respiratory-tract temperatures and are recurrently detected in mammalian-adapted clade 2.3.4.4b genotypes, making them closely watched risk markers. Recent genotypes circulating in North American dairy cattle and companion animals, including B3.13 and D1.1, carry constellations of such adaptive markers, and ongoing genomic surveillance by joint WHO/FAO/WOAH assessment continues to track their evolution for signals of increased mammalian or human transmissibility (Food and Agriculture Organization et al., 2025a; Man et al., 2026). Because most reassortant or drift-variant genotypes carry fitness costs that limit onward spread, only a minority of spillover events establish sustained transmission chains in a new host — but the frequency of coinfection opportunities, and hence the statistical opportunity for a high-fitness variant to emerge, rises directly with the scale of the current panzootic. This technical surveillance information, while central to expert risk assessment, is rarely rendered in a form accessible to non-specialist audiences, a gap addressed later in this review.These molecular determinants of host range and transmissibility are not simply of virological interest. Because receptor-binding adaptation, polymerase mutation, and reassortment are the specific mechanisms that determine whether a spillover event remains a dead-end infection or acquires the capacity for onward transmission, they define the biological rationale for the tiered, exposure-specific communication framework proposed in Section 7: household guidance calibrated to the animal-contact pathways — raw feeding, wild-bird contact, dairy exposure — most likely to provide the coinfection or exposure opportunities described above. Framing the practical framework in these molecular terms is intended to keep the proposed nursing role anchored to virological evidence rather than to a generic exhortation to be alert to ‘bird flu’. 3.Current epidemiological landscape: global panzootic and the Norwegian contextSince its emergence in Europe in 2020–2021, clade 2.3.4.4b has become globally dominant, spreading across Europe, Africa, the Americas, and, more recently, Antarctica, with unprecedented mortality events in wild bird and marine mammal populations (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 2025b; Kamel et al., 2025). The detection of the virus in United States dairy cattle in March 2024 marked a further expansion: as of mid-2025, outbreaks had been confirmed in more than 1,000 herds across multiple states, with clinical signs in cattle including decreased milk yield, abnormal milk consistency, and reduced feed intake (Food and Agriculture Organization et al., 2025a; Morel et al., 2026). Between March 2024 and May 2025, a total of approximately 70 human cases of HPAI A(H5) infection were reported in the United States: 41 following exposure to infected dairy cattle, 24 to commercial poultry, two to backyard poultry flocks, and three with undetermined exposure (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 2025c). Most infections presented as mild conjunctivitis, occasionally accompanied by fever or respiratory symptoms; a minority required hospitalization, and one death occurred in a person with underlying health conditions exposed to a backyard flock and wild birds (Rolfes et al., 2025). A first pediatric case with an undetermined exposure source was identified in California in late 2024 (Zhu et al., 2025).Companion animals have emerged as an additional and household-relevant transmission pathway. Domestic cats appear highly susceptible to severe, often fatal, disease, typically following consumption of raw milk, raw pet food, or contact with infected wild birds; a global review identified more than 600 documented feline infections across 12 species and 18 countries since the emergence of clade 2.3.4.4b (CIDRAP, 2025; Sykes, 2025). In late 2024, a cluster investigation in Los Angeles County identified serologic evidence consistent with possible virus transmission from an infected domestic cat to a veterinary professional — one of 25 serosurveyed contacts among 139 potentially exposed persons, with no virus isolated from the human case — providing what may be the first, if unconfirmed, instance of cat-to-human zoonotic transmission for this clade (Vaughan et al., 2026). To date, no sustained human-to-human transmission of clade 2.3.4.4b viruses has been documented anywhere, and joint WHO/FAO/WOAH and European risk assessments continue to classify general population risk as low, with elevated risk restricted to those with direct occupational or household exposure to infected animals (World Health Organization, 2025–2026; European Commission / EFSA).Within this global picture, Norway has not been spared. Norwegian Veterinary Institute wild-bird and mammalian surveillance programs document recurrent clade 2.3.4.4b detections, including spillover into Norwegian foxes and seals, consistent with broader European surveillance trends reported by the European Food Safety Authority and European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (Ytrehus et al; European Food Safety Authority et al., 2025a). As elsewhere, the general population risk in Norway is assessed as low, with the principal exposure pathway concentrated among individuals with occupational or hobbyist contact with wild birds, backyard poultry, or other domestic animals (Food and Agriculture Organization et al., 2025a) — a demographic that includes a meaningful proportion of Norwegian households with children, particularly in rural and peri-urban districts. 4.One health governance and pandemic preparedness in NorwayNorway has formally embedded One Health principles — the recognition that human, animal, and environmental health are interdependent — into its national approach to zoonotic disease and pandemic preparedness. The Norwegian Institute of Public Health identifies zoonotic influenza explicitly as a priority One Health working area, alongside food safety and antimicrobial resistance, and coordinates closely with the Norwegian Veterinary Institute and Norwegian Food Safety Authority on surveillance and risk communication (Norwegian Institute of Public Health (FHI), 2020). This institutional commitment is further reflected in Norway’s National One Health Strategy against Antimicrobial Resistance 2024–2033, which establishes cross-sectoral governance mechanisms that could, in principle, extend to influenza preparedness (Norwegian Ministry of Health and Care Services), and in an independent country-profile assessment noting that Norway has integrated One Health principles into its broader pandemic preparedness and response framework through interdisciplinary task forces and improved cross-sector data sharing (BeReady4Pandemics, 2025).Notably, however, these governance frameworks are articulated predominantly at the level of surveillance coordination and inter-agency data sharing among human, animal, and environmental health authorities. None of the reviewed strategy or preparedness documents specify a defined role for frontline, community-based health personnel in the direct translation of One Health surveillance findings into household-level guidance. This represents an implementation gap between governance-level One Health ambition and the last-mile communication needed to change everyday behavior — a gap this review argues the helsesykepleier workforce is structurally well placed to help close. 5.The helsesykepleier as a one health communication nodeHelsesykepleiere are specialist public health nurses operating within Norway’s statutorily mandated child health and school health services (helsestasjons- og skolehelsetjenesten), providing near-universal, longitudinal contact with children and families from infancy through upper secondary school, encompassing routine health checks, vaccination programs, and structured health guidance for parents and, later, directly for adolescents (Helsedirektoratet, 2021). This combination of near-total population reach, repeated contact over many years, and an existing mandate for preventive health counselling distinguishes the helsesykepleier role from generic public health messaging: unlike a one-off media campaign, the relationship is relational and cumulative, allowing guidance to be tailored to a given family’s actual animal exposures — for example, backyard poultry keeping, pet ownership, or proximity to wild-bird habitats — rather than delivered as an undifferentiated general warning.This structural advantage is particularly relevant given documented deficits in existing zoonotic-disease literacy…

title_original: From molecular evolution to the school health room: the role of community-based public health nurses (helsesykepleiere) in one health communication on cross-species influenza transmission in Norway

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the role of community-based public health nurses in translating virological and epidemiological evidence on cross-species influenza transmission into actionable public health communication for children, adolescents, and families in Norway. This is critical given the documented gaps in adolescent One Health literacy and the need for improved risk communication.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a mini review analyzing the molecular basis of influenza cross-species transmission, the Norwegian epidemiological and One Health governance context, and child- and family-oriented risk-communication frameworks. It focuses on the role of community-based public health nurses (helsesykepleiere) in Norway, who provide near-universal contact with children and families through the helsestasjon- and skolehelsetjeneste.
analysis.methods: The methods involved synthesizing current literature on molecular determinants of host range and transmissibility, reviewing the Norwegian One Health governance context, and examining established risk-communication frameworks for children and families. The study also analyzed surveillance data and institutional commitments to zoonotic influenza preparedness.
analysis.main_results: The study reports that clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have become globally dominant, with recurrent detections in Norwegian wild-bird and mammalian surveillance programs, including spillover into foxes and seals. It also highlights the detection of these viruses in U.S. dairy cattle and companion animals, with documented human cases of HPAI A(H5) infection linked to animal exposure.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the helsesykepleiere, due to their near-universal contact with children and families, are uniquely positioned to translate One Health surveillance findings into household-level guidance. This is a novel perspective on leveraging community-based health personnel for effective risk communication.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that integrating community-based public health nurses into One Health communication frameworks could improve family-level understanding and protective behavior against zoonotic influenza, particularly in the context of the ongoing global panzootic of clade 2.3.4.4b viruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a mini review of existing literature and surveillance data, which may limit the depth of analysis. However, the evidence is grounded in documented epidemiological trends and institutional commitments, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the role of community-based public health nurses in Norway in translating virological and epidemiological evidence on cross-species influenza transmission into actionable public health communication for children, adolescents, and families. It highlights the global dominance of clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, their spillover into Norwegian wildlife, and the detection of these viruses in U.S. dairy cattle and companion animals, with documented human cases linked to animal exposure. The authors argue that these nurses, with their near-universal contact with families, are uniquely positioned to improve risk communication and understanding of zoonotic influenza. However, the study is limited to a review of existing literature and surveillance data, and it notes that current governance frameworks do not explicitly define a role for these nurses in influenza preparedness. The findings suggest that integrating these nurses into One Health communication could enhance family-level protective behaviors, but further evaluation research is needed to confirm this. The evidence is moderate in strength due to its reliance on secondary sources and the absence of direct experimental data.
